TITLE: Rachel Reeves drops push for food price cap after retail backlash
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-20
SOURCE: Financial Times

KEY:
- Treasury effort to persuade UK supermarkets to agree voluntary food price caps has been dropped after retail backlash
- Retail sources rebuffed government proposal as "unjustified" and likely to push costs up across the board
- Independent: framed as "Soviet-style price caps"
- The Times: "Supermarket grocery prices could freeze to tackle soaring inflation rates" (Wednesday paper preview)
- Sainsbury's (per Reuters April 23): had called for UK government to support food sector to offset high energy costs from Iran war

GUARDIAN PARALLEL (Tuesday):
- Voluntary price cap proposal was for 20-50 essential items (eggs, bread, milk)
- SNP pledged to use devolved public health powers to fix prices in Scotland

CONTEXT:
- Iran war driving food inflation
- Brent at $106.40 Wednesday morning, eased from $110+ peak
- The U-turn drop on price caps is part of the same Wednesday news cycle as fuel duty freeze + haulier vehicle tax holiday
- Treasury net cost of fuel duty + haulier package: ~£400m
